The black hollow tissue in the image is the **airway**, specifically the **trachea** (windpipe), which appears as a dark, circular structure in the center of the axial CT scan of the neck.

In CT imaging, air appears black (hypodense) because it has very low attenuation (low density) compared to soft tissues and bone. The trachea is a hollow organ that contains air, which is why it shows up as a dark circle in this cross-sectional view.

This is normal anatomy — the trachea is present in the neck region and is clearly visible here.
